operational_nodes.name: AC_01_Pure_Schema_Driven_Symbol_Derivation
operational_nodes.doc: - **Given:** An input schema source $`\mathcal{S}`$ containing user-defined declarations (`Package_0`, `Classifier_Alpha`, `Port_1`) and standard compiler grammar tokens $``\mathcal{K}_{\text{grammar}}``$. - **When:** The compiler executes the front-end ingestion and AST construction pass $`\mathcal{C} : \mathcal{S} \longrightarrow \mathcal{A}`$. - **Then:** Every symbol $`\sigma \in \text{Symbols}(\mathcal{A})`$ resolves strictly to $``\text{Tokens}(\mathcal{S}) \cup \mathcal{K}_{\text{grammar}} \cup \text{Synthetic}(\mathcal{S})``$, guaranteeing zero ungrounded or fabricated identifiers. - **Diagnostic:** `E0100` emitted on any symbol failing positive set containment.

operational_nodes.name: AC_02_Zero_Domain_Vocabulary_Contamination
operational_nodes.doc: - **Given:** An arbitrary schema $`\mathcal{S}`$ compiled against standard lowering rules, code generators, and intermediate representation emitters. - **When:** The AST validation pass evaluates $`\text{Symbols}(\mathcal{A})`$ against predefined domain vocabularies $``\mathcal{V}_{\text{domain\_hardcoded}}``$. - **Then:** The intersection $``\text{Symbols}(\mathcal{A}) \cap \mathcal{V}_{\text{domain\_hardcoded}} = \emptyset``$ holds identically, ensuring zero hardcoded domain nouns or concrete domain assumptions. - **Diagnostic:** `E0100` emitted if any AST symbol references a prohibited domain dictionary entry.

operational_nodes.name: AC_03_Deterministic_RFC_4122_UUIDv5_Topological_Path_Anchors
operational_nodes.doc: - **Given:** A structural AST node with canonical topological path $`p \in \text{TopologicalPaths}(\mathcal{S})`$ (e.g., `Package_0::Classifier_Alpha::Port_1`). - **When:** The compiler synthesizes a node identifier or document anchor. - **Then:** The generated identifier matches $``\text{UUIDv5}(\text{NS}_{\text{DEAP}}, p)``$ with version bits $``(u_6 \land 0\text{xF0}) = 0\text{x50}``$ and variant bits $``(u_8 \land 0\text{xC0}) = 0\text{x80}``$, invariant across execution hosts, environments, and timestamps. - **Diagnostic:** `E0100` emitted on UUIDv5 computation failure or bitwise variant mismatch.

operational_nodes.name: AC_04_Bitwise_Determinism_across_Repeated_Invocations
operational_nodes.doc: - **Given:** Two identical input schema token streams $``\mathcal{S}_1``$ and $``\mathcal{S}_2``$ such that $``\mathcal{S}_1 = \mathcal{S}_2``$. - **When:** The compilation pipeline $`\mathcal{C}`$ executes in isolated environments or independent process invocations. - **Then:** The resulting AST models and emitted byte streams satisfy $``\mathcal{C}(\mathcal{S}_1) = \mathcal{C}(\mathcal{S}_2)``$ with 0-byte diff churn. - **Diagnostic:** `E0100` emitted if serialized outputs diverge across repeated compilations of identical inputs. --- *Traceability: Elaborated under IEEE 29148-2018 and the DEAP Compiler Streamlined Charter.*

operational_nodes.name: _1_Normative_Statement
operational_nodes.doc: The compiler platform shall function strictly as an abstract Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) compiler, deriving all synthesized intermediate representations, verification models, downstream specification projections, and interface definitions deterministically from user-provided schema inputs. The compiler must operate exclusively on generic systems engineering metamodel primitives: Classifiers, Feature Usages, Abstract Ports, Directional Connectors, Mathematical Constraints, Discrete State Transitions, and Occurrence Lifecycles. Compilation passes, lowering pipelines, code generators, and autonomous tooling agents are strictly prohibited from hardcoding, injecting, or assuming domain-specific concepts, domain vocabularies, or heuristic domain assumptions into pipeline logic, templates, intermediate representations, or emitted artifacts. All illustrative examples, test fixtures, and internal representations shall utilize purely synthetic abstract placeholders (e.g., `Package_0`, `Classifier_Alpha`, `Port_1`, `Flow_A`, `param_x : Real`). When synthetic structural identifiers or topological anchors are generated for intermediate representations or scaffolding nodes, they shall be deterministically derived via RFC 4122 UUIDv5 namespace hashing rooted in a fixed compiler namespace UUID constant ($``\text{NS}_{\text{DEAP}}``$) and the fully qualified topological path of the element within the abstract syntax tree containment hierarchy. If any compilation stage detects an ungrounded domain term or non-schema symbol outside the formal grammar vocabulary and synthetic anchor set, the compiler shall halt execution immediately and emit diagnostic error code `E0100`. ---

operational_nodes.name: _2_Formal_Invariant
operational_nodes.doc: Let $`\mathcal{S}`$ denote the set of input schema tokens and $``\mathcal{K}_{\text{grammar}}``$ denote the fixed vocabulary of compiler grammar keywords. Let $`\text{Symbols}(\mathcal{A})`$ denote the set of all symbol identifiers present in synthesized abstract syntax tree $`\mathcal{A}`$. Let $`\text{TopologicalPaths}(\mathcal{S})`$ denote the set of fully qualified topological paths derived from $`\mathcal{S}`$, and let $``\text{NS}_{\text{DEAP}} \in \{0, 1\}^{128}``$ denote the fixed RFC 4122 namespace UUID constant. Universal Symbol Grounding Invariant: \forall \sigma \in \text{Symbols}(\mathcal{A}), \quad \sigma \in \text{Tokens}(\mathcal{S}) \cup \mathcal{K}_{\text{grammar}} \cup \text{Synthetic}(\mathcal{S}) where synthetic symbols derive deterministically via RFC 4122 UUIDv5 topological path hashing: \text{Synthetic}(\mathcal{S}) = \{ \text{UUIDv5}(\text{NS}_{\text{DEAP}}, p) \mid p \in \text{TopologicalPaths}(\mathcal{S}) \} Deterministic Pipeline Mapping Invariant: The compiler pipeline execution is modeled as a total deterministic mapping $`\mathcal{C}`$: \mathcal{C} : \mathcal{S} \longrightarrow \mathcal{A} such that identical input schema token streams yield identical abstract syntax tree structures: \forall \mathcal{S}_1, \mathcal{S}_2, \quad \mathcal{S}_1 = \mathcal{S}_2 \implies \mathcal{C}(\mathcal{S}_1) = \mathcal{C}(\mathcal{S}_2) Zero Hardcoded Domain Concepts Invariant: Let $``\mathcal{V}_{\text{domain\_hardcoded}}``$ represent any predefined domain-specific terminology, domain ontology, or non-schema concept dictionary. The synthesized AST satisfies: \text{Symbols}(\mathcal{A}) \cap \mathcal{V}_{\text{domain\_hardcoded}} = \emptyset Synthetic Identifier RFC 4122 Bit Invariant: For each synthetic identifier $``U = \text{UUIDv5}(\text{NS}_{\text{DEAP}}, p) = (u_0, u_1, \dots, u_{15}) \in (\mathbb{Z}_{256})^{16}``$, the version and variant fields satisfy: \begin{aligned} (u_6 \land 0\text{xF0}) &= 0\text{x50} \\ (u_8 \land 0\text{xC0}) &= 0\text{x80} \end{aligned} ---

operational_nodes.name: _3_Computational_Complexity_Algorithmic_Bounds
operational_nodes.doc: The compilation pipeline operates within Complexity Class $`\mathbf{P}`$. Token scanning, symbol table interning, and schema set membership verification execute in deterministic linear time $`O(N)`$ with respect to total input schema token count $`N = |\text{Tokens}(\mathcal{S})|`$. Synthetic topological anchor generation and path hashing execute in $`O(V + E)`$ where $`V = |\text{Nodes}(\mathcal{A})|`$ and $`E = |\text{Edges}(\mathcal{A})|`$ represent AST hierarchy vertices and containment edges. Foundational schema ingestion and validation require no combinatorial search, bypassing NP-hard frontiers (e.g., NP-1 through NP-8) and guaranteeing total-function polynomial termination. ---
